def exchange(lst1, lst2):
    """In this problem, you will implement a function that takes two lists of numbers,
    and determines whether it is possible to perform exchanges to make lst1 
    a list of only even numbers.
    Elements can be exchanged between lst1 and lst2 to achieve this goal.
    If it is possible to make all the elements of lst1 even through exchanges, 
    return "YES". Otherwise, return "NO".
    """

Clarification: Yes -- there is no limit on the number of exchanged elements between lst1 and lst2, and the exchange is not required to be a strict one-to-one swap; any elements can be moved between the two lists as needed to make all of lst1's elements even.

Clarification: Only exchanged -- the reference never adds or removes elements from either list; it counts odd elements in lst1 and even elements in lst2, and checks whether there are enough even elements in lst2 to swap in for every odd element in lst1 (even >= odd), preserving both lists' sizes.
question: Can the function exchange elements between lst1 and lst2 in any way as long as the final lst1 contains only even numbers, or are there specific rules about which elements can be swapped?
answer: There's no literal element-by-element swap simulated -- per the reference, the function only compares counts: the number of odd elements in lst1 versus the number of even elements available in lst2. If lst2 has at least as many even elements as lst1 has odd elements, it's considered feasible ('YES'), regardless of which specific elements would be paired.
